name: Alexander
conditionCost: Must stay at war to keep the engine running
note: No war weariness is only worth anything while at war. Peace turns the kit off.

civInfo.name: Alexander

leader_ability.name: To the World's End
leader_ability.text: Removes war weariness in Alexander's cities, heals his units when he captures a city containing a Wonder, and unlocks his unique Hetairoi heavy cavalry unit, supporting a strategy of continuous, far-flung conquest without the usual unhappiness penalties.

agenda.name: Short Life of Glory
agenda.text: Alexander favors civilizations that are at war with someone other than himself and dislikes those at peace; in Gathering Storm, Grievances against him also decay twice as fast as normal.

civ_ability.name: Hellenistic Fusion
civ_ability.text: When Macedon captures a foreign city, it gains a bonus tied to the types of Districts already present there, letting Alexander's empire absorb and benefit from the specializations of conquered territory rather than razing them.

unique_units.name: Hetairoi
unique_units.notes: A powerful heavy cavalry unit unlocked by Alexander's leader ability, giving Macedon an early mounted strike force well ahead of other civilizations.

unique_units.name: Hypaspist
unique_units.notes: Gains a combat bonus when attacking districts and cities, making Macedon especially effective at siege and city capture.

unique_infrastructure.name: Basilikoi Paides
unique_infrastructure.replaces_note: replaces the Barracks, built in the Encampment district
unique_infrastructure.notes: Boosts Production, Housing, and combat experience for units trained in the city, and grants Science based on the cost of units produced, tying Macedon's military machine to both growth and research.

civInfo.historical_background: Alexander the Great became king of Macedon in 336 BCE and, within thirteen years, conquered the entire Persian Empire, extending Macedonian rule from Greece to Egypt and northwest India before his death at age 32 in 323 BCE. His conquests spread Greek (Hellenistic) language, art, and institutions across the ancient world, blending with local cultures in the regions he took — the direct inspiration for Macedon's civ ability, which lets the empire absorb bonuses from captured cities rather than simply destroying them. After his death his generals, the Diadochi, carved his empire into rival successor kingdoms, and his relentless campaigning without ever losing a battle is echoed by his agenda's restless preference for a civilization always at war.

context.condition_cost: Must stay at war to keep the engine running

era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Continuous war with no domestic penalty.
era_role.industrial_modern: Still warring, but tech parity becomes the binding constraint.

context.off_period_plan: There should be no off period by design; if peace lasts more than a few turns, that itself is the amber signal

template.principle: The core loop is a stat check, not a build order. These guides fail hardest when written as sequences, because the player's real job is watching one number and responding to it.

structure.goal: Establish the thing being monitored and the infrastructure that lets you respond to it.
steps: Name the watched stat on turn 1: Current war/peace state and next-target readiness
Establish its bands before it matters, so the player recognizes trouble the first time rather than the third.
Build the response capacity. A monitor with no available response is just anxiety.

structure.goal: This replaces the turn list entirely. The guide is this loop plus the era checkpoints.
per_turn_check: Read Current war/peace state and next-target readiness.
Green band: continue current build. No action.
Amber band: begin the correction now. Amber is the acting band; red is the failing band.
Red band: the ability is off or about to be. Everything else is deprioritized until it clears.
structure.opportunity_trigger: For reactive leaders (Lautaro, Tamar, John Curtin), add a second watched value: the external condition that switches the ability on. The guide must state what to do during the periods it is off, because those periods are most of the game.

structure.goal: Re-read the role. Monitor leaders change what the stat means across eras.
steps: Ancient/Classical: Encampment build-out and first wars.
Medieval/Renaissance: Peak. Continuous war with no domestic penalty.
Industrial/Modern: Still warring, but tech parity becomes the binding constraint.
Atomic/Information: Functional, no longer special.

abort_branch.trigger: Watched stat sits in the red band for more than roughly 15 turns with no recovery path.
actions: Stop paying the Must stay at war to keep the engine running. If the bonus is unreachable, its price is pure loss.
Rebuild as a generic civ around whatever the monitored strategy already produced.

template.fail_state: The stat crossed into red and stayed. For Alexander, Peace switches the kit off. There is no reward for consolidation phases.
anti_patterns: Writing this shape as a turn-by-turn build order. It is the wrong instrument.

name: Amanitore
conditionCost: Nubian Pyramids want desert-adjacent placement
note: Dual-banks: conquest AND permanently cheaper districts. Survives its own spike better than most.

civInfo.name: Amanitore

leader_ability.name: Kandake of Meroë
leader_ability.text: Cities gain a solid Production bonus toward Districts, which increases further in cities where a Nubian Pyramid is adjacent to the City Center, pushing Nubia toward rapid, district-heavy cities.

agenda.name: City Planner
agenda.text: Amanitore tries to build as many districts as possible in her cities and favors other leaders who also prioritize dense district development.

civ_ability.name: Ta-Seti
civ_ability.text: Nubia gets extra Production toward Ranged units, and those units earn combat experience faster than normal. Mines also yield bonus Production on strategic resources and bonus Gold on luxury resources, tying the civilization's military and economic strength together.

unique_units.name: Pitati Archer
unique_units.notes: A stronger, faster Ancient-era ranged unit that synergizes with Nubia's Ranged-unit production and experience bonuses for early ranged-rush strategies.

unique_infrastructure.name: Nubian Pyramid
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement (unlocked with Masonry) that generates Faith and gains extra yields when placed next to the City Center or other districts, rewarding compact, district-rich cities.

civInfo.historical_background: Amanitore was a Kandake (ruling queen) of the Kingdom of Kush, centered at Meroë in what is now Sudan, reigning in the 1st century CE alongside her co-ruler Natakamani. Nubian kandakes held real political and sometimes military authority, a tradition distinct from many neighboring cultures, and several are remembered leading armies in defense of their kingdom. Amanitore and Natakamani presided over an extensive building program, constructing and restoring temples and pyramids at Meroë, Naqa, and elsewhere, which is echoed in-game by the civilization's pyramid improvement and its strong bias toward dense urban district construction.

era_role.medieval_renaissance: Infrastructure snowball off permanently cheaper districts.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong generic empire; the military identity is long gone.

Caesar's brutal reprisal campaign nearly exterminated the Eburones, though Ambiorix himself reportedly escaped and vanished from history. He is remembered today, especially in Belgium, as an early symbol of resistance to Roman conquest, directly reflected in his in-game agenda 'Scourge of Rome' and his ability rewarding militarization and unit concentration reminiscent of guerrilla-style Gallic warfare.

civInfo.name: Ba Trieu
civInfo.leader_title: Lady Trieu, folk heroine of Vietnamese resistance

leader_ability.name: Drive Out The Aggressors
leader_ability.text: Vietnamese units gain bonus Movement and Combat Strength while on Woods, Rainforest, or Marsh tiles, with the bonus doubled when those tiles are inside Vietnam's own territory, making Vietnam extremely strong at defending its jungle terrain against invasion.

agenda.name: Defender of the Homeland
agenda.text: Ba Trieu favors civilizations that have never declared war on Vietnam, and permanently distrusts and dislikes any civilization that ever has, regardless of how much time has passed.

civ_ability.name: Nine Dragon River Delta
civ_ability.text: Vietnam can only place specialty land districts on Woods, Rainforest, or Marsh tiles, but buildings in those districts gain bonus Culture, Science, or Production depending on the terrain feature, turning a placement restriction into a themed yield bonus.

unique_units.name: Voi Chiến
unique_units.notes: A Medieval ranged unit with more Movement and Sight than the Crossbowman, and the ability to move after attacking, well suited to Vietnam's mobile jungle-terrain warfare.

unique_infrastructure.name: Thành
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Encampment; provides bonus Culture for each adjacent district and, once Flight is researched, converts that Culture output into Tourism, giving Vietnam a militarized district with a late-game culture payoff.

civInfo.historical_background: Triệu Thị Trinh, known as Bà Triệu ('Lady Trieu'), was a 3rd-century CE Vietnamese woman who led an armed rebellion against occupying Chinese (Eastern Wu) rule around 248 CE. Vietnamese tradition holds she declared she would rather 'ride the wind and walk the waves' and fight as a warrior than live bowed under foreign rule as a servant, and though her rebellion was ultimately crushed, she became -- alongside the earlier Trung Sisters -- one of Vietnam's most enduring symbols of resistance to foreign domination. That legacy of guerrilla resistance fought from Vietnam's dense terrain against a more powerful invader directly informs her in-game kit, which rewards fighting from (and defending) Vietnam's woods, rainforest, and marsh tiles and never forgives a civilization that has declared war on her.

name: Basil II
conditionCost: Requires founding a religion AND spreading it to the target first
note: Two-step prerequisite before the combat bonus exists. Slow to come online, brutal once it does.

civInfo.name: Basil II

leader_ability.name: Porphyrogénnētos
leader_ability.text: Basil's heavy and light cavalry units deal full damage when attacking cities that follow the same religion as Byzantium, and researching Divine Right unlocks his powerful unique Tagma unit, rewarding a combined religious-military conquest strategy.

agenda.name: Divine Guardian
agenda.text: Basil II focuses on spreading his religion and defending it, favoring civilizations that share his faith and disliking those that follow a different one.

civ_ability.name: Taxis
civ_ability.text: Byzantine units gain bonus Combat and Religious Strength for every Holy City following Byzantium's religion (including its own), Byzantium's religion spreads automatically when an enemy unit is defeated in combat, and Holy Site cities earn extra Great Prophet points.

unique_units.name: Tagma
unique_units.notes: Unlocked via Basil's leader ability upon researching Divine Right; it grants Combat or Religious Strength to nearby friendly land units, functioning as a mobile support unit as well as a strong attacker.

unique_units.name: Dromon
unique_units.notes: A naval melee unit with greater range and combat strength than the Quadrireme, giving Byzantium an early naval edge.

unique_infrastructure.name: Hippodrome
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Entertainment Complex, costs less Production, grants extra Amenities, and spawns a free Heavy Cavalry unit each time the district or one of its buildings is completed.

civInfo.historical_background: Basil II (reigned 976-1025) was one of the Byzantine Empire's most formidable emperors, expanding its borders to their greatest extent since Justinian through decades of relentless campaigning, most famously his prolonged conquest of the First Bulgarian Empire, which earned him the epithet 'Bulgar-Slayer.' Born 'porphyrogennetos' ('born in the purple'), meaning born to a reigning emperor in the palace's porphyry chamber, he ruled as a soldier-emperor who tied military success closely to Orthodox Christian identity and left the treasury and empire stronger than he found them. His fusion of religious authority with battlefield conquest is captured directly in his leader ability's name and its focus on converting military victories into religious dominance.

tests: Gate open AND staging complete: proceed to Post-Gate.

expansionOrigin: Base Game (Black Queen is Catherine's original/default persona; the alternate 'Magnificence' persona was added later via New Frontier Pass Persona Packs)
conditionCost: None

civInfo.name: Catherine de Medici (Black Queen)
civInfo.expansion_origin: Base Game (Black Queen is Catherine's original/default persona; the alternate 'Magnificence' persona was added later via New Frontier Pass Persona Packs)

leader_ability.name: Catherine's Flying Squadron
leader_ability.text: As the Black Queen persona (her default, original ability), Catherine gains one extra level of Diplomatic Visibility with every civilization she has met, receives a free Spy upon researching Castles, and all her Spies start with a free promotion — making her the strongest espionage leader in the game. (Her alternate Magnificence persona instead focuses on collecting and trading Luxury resources via the agenda 'Sumptuous Finery.')

agenda.name: Black Queen
agenda.text: Catherine wants to accumulate as many Spies and as much Diplomatic Visibility as possible, and dislikes leaders who ignore espionage entirely.

civ_ability.name: Grand Tour
civ_ability.text: France gets bonus Production toward Medieval, Renaissance, and Industrial era Wonders, and doubles the Tourism generated by Wonders of any era, making France one of the strongest wonder-rush/culture-victory civilizations.

unique_units.name: Garde Impériale
unique_units.replaces: Line Infantry (later replaces the Musketman-tier military unit chain)
unique_units.notes: An Industrial era melee unit with higher base Combat Strength and a large bonus fighting on the capital's home continent, plus Great General points from kills.

unique_infrastructure.name: Château
unique_infrastructure.notes: Must be built adjacent to a river and provides Culture, with bonus Culture the closer it is to a Wonder, reinforcing France's wonder-and-culture strategy.

civInfo.historical_background: Catherine de' Medici (1519-1589) was an Italian-born queen consort and later regent of France during the tumultuous French Wars of Religion, wielding influence over her sons' reigns as king. She earned a fearsome reputation — fairly or not — for court intrigue, poison plots, and involvement in events like the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre, cementing the 'Black Queen' legend that names her default in-game persona and its espionage/spy focus. Her family's Medici banking and political dynasty in Florence also connects to her later New Frontier persona, 'Magnificence,' which instead emphasizes courtly luxury and the collection of fine resources, echoing the opulent Medici court culture.

civInfo.name: Cyrus

leader_ability.name: Fall of Babylon

civInfo.historical_background: Cyrus II, known as Cyrus the Great, founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire in the mid-6th century BCE, rapidly conquering the Median, Lydian, and Neo-Babylonian empires (including the fall of Babylon referenced in his leader ability) to create the largest empire the world had yet seen. He was noted for relatively tolerant governance of conquered peoples, exemplified by the Cyrus Cylinder, and for a career built on swift, decisive military campaigns — reflected in his ability's rewards for surprise warfare. Cyrus was ultimately killed in 530 BCE in battle against Tomyris and the Massagetae, a fitting rival matchup within Civilization VI given her leader ability is literally named for his death.

Carthage's power rested on an extensive network of coastal colonies and trade routes stretching across the Mediterranean, a legacy that eventually put it in prolonged conflict with Greek city-states in Sicily and, later, with Rome in the Punic Wars. Her legendary founding of a new city by the sea and Phoenicia's historical mastery of coastal colonization directly shape both her capital-relocating leader ability and the civilization's emphasis on rapid, loyal coastal settlement.

civInfo.historical_background: John Curtin served as Australia's Prime Minister from 1941 to 1945, leading the country through the most direct existential threat it had faced: the Japanese advance through the Pacific during World War II, including air raids on Darwin and the fall of Singapore. He died in office in July 1945, shortly before the war's end, worn down by the strain of wartime leadership. His defining legacy of turning a defensive crisis into national mobilization and a lasting policy of forming strong external alliances is reflected directly in his in-game kit's war-triggered production bonuses and preference for Defensive Pacts.

agenda.name: Bibliophile
agenda.text: Kristina tries to collect as many Great Works as possible and likes leaders who leave Great Works for her to acquire; she dislikes rivals who compete hard for the same Great Works.

unique_units.name: Carolean
unique_units.notes: A Renaissance era unit with extra Movement and a Combat Strength bonus for each point of unused Movement, plus bonus strength against cavalry, rewarding aggressive, mobile play.

civInfo.historical_background: Kristina (1626-1689) was Queen of Sweden from 1632 to 1654, a famously erudite and unconventional monarch who turned Stockholm into a hub for scholars, philosophers (including René Descartes, who died there), and artists, earning Sweden the nickname 'Athens of the North' during her reign — the direct inspiration for her in-game 'Minerva of the North' ability and Great Works focus. She abdicated the throne in 1654, converted to Catholicism (a controversial act for a Lutheran monarch), and spent much of her later life in Rome as a patron of the arts and sciences. Her personal passion for collecting books, art, and manuscripts is reflected in Sweden's Great Works/Bibliophile-centered kit.

leader_ability.text: Kupe begins the game embarked on the Ocean rather than on land, earning +2 Science and +2 Culture per turn before he founds his first city. Founding that first city grants a free Builder and +1 Population, and his Palace provides extra Housing and an Amenity, smoothing the unusual late, ocean-based start.

agenda.name: Kaitiakitanga
agenda.text: Kupe preserves natural features and builds National Parks; he likes civilizations that respect the environment (avoiding harvesting and terrain removal) and dislikes those who despoil it.

civ_ability.name: Mana
civ_ability.text: The Māori start with Sailing and Shipbuilding and can move directly onto Ocean tiles from the outset. Their embarked units gain bonus Combat Strength and Movement, unimproved Woods and Rainforest tiles yield bonus Production, and Fishing Boats grant extra Food and trigger a Culture Bomb, making the Māori strong at settling and expanding across open ocean.

unique_units.name: Toa
unique_units.notes: A Classical era melee unit that can build the defensive Pā improvement on hills and weakens adjacent enemy units with a Haka war dance, giving the Māori solid mid-game defense despite their peaceful, exploration-focused kit.

unique_infrastructure.name: Marae
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Amphitheater in the Theater Square; it grants Culture and Faith from every passable feature (e.g., Woods, Floodplains) in the city and Tourism after Flight, rewarding a Māori empire that keeps its natural terrain intact.

civInfo.historical_background: Kupe is a legendary Polynesian navigator credited in Māori oral tradition with being one of the first explorers to discover and name Aotearoa (New Zealand), guiding a great ocean-going waka (canoe) across the Pacific using wayfinding by stars, currents, and birds. As a figure of oral history rather than documented record, his exact dates are unknown, but he is central to Māori foundational narratives of migration and settlement. His in-game role as an ocean-starting leader who arrives to found cities directly mirrors this voyaging legend, and the Māori civilization's environmental, ocean-adjacency-focused kit reflects traditional Māori concepts of kaitiakitanga (guardianship of nature).

civ_ability.name: Mayab

unique_units.name: Hul'che
unique_units.notes: An Ancient-era ranged unit with higher Ranged Strength than the Archer and a bonus against already-wounded units, giving the Maya strong early skirmishing power, especially near the Capital where Lady Six Sky's ability adds further Combat Strength.

unique_infrastructure.name: Observatory
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Campus; gets a major Science bonus from each adjacent Plantation and a minor bonus from adjacent Farms or districts, tying neatly into the Maya's farm-focused civilization ability.

civInfo.historical_background: Lady Six Sky was a Maya queen who arrived at the city-state of Naranjo (in present-day Guatemala) around 682 CE and is credited with reviving it after a period of military defeat and decline, quite possibly having come from the powerful city of Dos Pilas or Calakmul. She oversaw military campaigns that restored Naranjo's regional power and, notably, placed her young son on the throne as king while continuing to wield significant authority herself, an unusual degree of female political power commemorated on Naranjo's carved stelae. That story of rebuilding and defending a single powerful city-state rather than pursuing distant conquest is mirrored directly in her in-game ability, which rewards a compact empire clustered tightly around the capital and penalizes overextension.

leader_ability.name: Swift Hawk

His guerrilla-style raiding tactics and refusal to hold static ground helped the Mapuche resist full Spanish conquest for centuries, longer than almost any other indigenous American people, a legacy echoed in his in-game focus on mobile raiding and loyalty-destabilizing warfare against more 'settled' golden-age rivals.

His reign saw Bavaria's political independence curtailed as Germany unified under Prussian leadership, and he died in disputed circumstances shortly after being declared mentally unfit to rule. His singular association with fabulous gold wealth built on desert trade routes is the direct inspiration for his Gold-obsessed agenda and Mali's desert-and-trade-focused civilization ability.

He is equally famous for the enormous Terracotta Army buried to guard his tomb, and for a harsh, centralizing rule that built lasting state infrastructure at great human cost. His fixation on grand unifying construction projects and standardization is mirrored in his in-game ability to rush Wonders and China's civilization-wide bonus for converting breakthroughs into further progress.

civInfo.historical_background: Seondeok reigned as Queen of Silla, one of Korea's Three Kingdoms, from 632 to 647 CE, becoming the first reigning queen in Korean history. She also strengthened Silla's diplomatic ties with Tang China during a period of intense rivalry among Korea's Three Kingdoms, groundwork that helped Silla eventually unify the peninsula after her reign. Her hallmark blend of scholarly patronage, astronomy, and governance is reflected in her in-game kit's emphasis on Science output and Governor-driven yield bonuses.

leader_ability.text: Suleiman gains access to a unique, exclusive Governor (Ibrahim) with strong military and diplomatic bonuses, and unlocks the Janissary unique unit plus a bonus Governor Title once Gunpowder is researched. agenda.text: Suleiman keeps his own cities happy and loyal, and is impressed by civilizations that do the same or have founded many cities; he dislikes leaders whose cities are unhappy, disloyal, or few in number due to conquest.

civInfo.historical_background: Suleiman I (r. 1520-1566) presided over the Ottoman Empire at its territorial and cultural zenith, pushing its borders deep into Hungary and the Middle East while his fleets contested the Mediterranean. His reign relied heavily on the elite, gunpowder-armed Janissary corps and an efficient siege-focused military, both reflected in the Ottomans' in-game strengths. This mix of centralizing governance and relentless military expansion is the throughline connecting the historical sultan to his in-game kit of governance-boosting abilities and siege-crushing bombards.

structure.goal: Reach the window with everything already staged. Nothing in this phase is optional; staging done after the window opens is spent from the budget.
steps: Turn 1: identify the target. Tomyris's window is short enough that target selection cannot wait for scouting to finish.
Turns 1-15: scout toward the target only. Exploration away from the target is a luxury this shape cannot afford.
Turns 10-30: production goes to the units or charges the window will consume. Infrastructure that pays back after 85 is deferred.
Pre-window checkpoint: confirm None is satisfied and units are within striking distance, not at home.

structure.goal: Convert tempo into permanent assets. Cities, wonders, or improvements. Not kills, not gold, not map presence.
core_loop: Each turn, ask: is the objective closer than it was last turn?
If the answer is no for three consecutive turns, the window is failing. Go to the abort branch.
Track remaining turns explicitly. The player should always know the number.

checkpoints.test: Is at least half the objective secured?
checkpoints.if_no: Reduce scope now. Take one city instead of three. Partial conversion beats total expiry.

checkpoints.test: Has the tempo become something permanent?

structure.goal: Stabilize what was taken. This phase is longer than both prior phases combined and most guides for this shape underwrite it badly.
steps: Amenity and loyalty audit on every acquired city before any new construction.
Infrastructure catch-up: the arming phase deliberately skipped this, and the bill comes due now.
Choose a victory path. Tomyris has no leader-specific direction from here; Ability contributes nothing.

abort_branch.trigger: Window closed with no permanent gain, or three stalled turns before the midpoint.
actions: Make peace immediately. Prolonging a failed window converts a bad position into a lost game.
Disband surplus units. The maintenance is now pure loss.
Switch to the generic development plan for the empire you actually have.

template.fail_state: The window closed and nothing permanent was gained. Tomyris is now an ordinary civ with an army it cannot afford and grievances it cannot repay.
anti_patterns: Writing Phase 3 as an afterthought. It is most of the game.
Expressing the deadline as a turn number only. Tie it to opponent tech where possible, since that is what actually closes the window.
Letting the player believe a large army at 85 counts as success. It does not.

name: Trajan
conditionCost: None
note: Free Monument in every city is the definition of a compounding, unconditional bonus. Beginner-safe.

civInfo.name: Trajan

leader_ability.name: Trajan's Column
leader_ability.text: Every city Trajan founds or acquires gets an extra free building in its City Center slot beyond the normal one (a Monument if still in the Ancient Era, or the era-appropriate equivalent later), giving Rome a permanent head start on infrastructure in every city, new or old.

agenda.name: Optimus Princeps
agenda.text: Trajan tries to bring as much territory as possible under his empire's control and looks down on civilizations that hold only a small amount of territory.

civ_ability.name: All Roads Lead to Rome
civ_ability.text: All Roman cities start with a free Trading Post, roads are automatically built to new cities within trade range of the Capital, and Gold income from Trade Routes passing through Roman cities is increased, giving Rome an economic and connectivity edge from the earliest turns.

unique_units.name: Legion
unique_units.notes: A stronger, more expensive Classical-era melee unit that doesn't require Iron and carries a builder charge it can spend to construct a Roman Fort, build a road, or harvest a resource in the field.

unique_infrastructure.name: Bath
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Aqueduct (must be built adjacent to the City Center and a water/mountain feature) and provides Amenities alongside its Housing bonus, making Rome's early cities more comfortable to grow.

civInfo.historical_background: Trajan ruled the Roman Empire from 98 to 117 AD and pushed it to its greatest territorial extent, conquering Dacia (for its gold) and campaigning into Mesopotamia and Armenia against Parthia. He is remembered as one of the 'Five Good Emperors' for combining military conquest with an ambitious building program: Trajan's Forum, Trajan's Market, and Trajan's Column (commemorating the Dacian Wars) all still stand in Rome today. His reputation for expanding territory while simultaneously building up infrastructure at home directly informs his in-game kit, which rewards both extra city buildings and holding maximal territory.

context.condition_cost: None

era_role.ancient_classical: Aggressive settling with free culture in every city.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Compounding civic lead from accumulated Monuments.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ordinary large empire; ability contribution is baked in already.
era_role.atomic_information: No ongoing effect, but the head start persists.

caveats: Free Monuments make expansion feel free. Amenities, gold, and loyalty are still real limits.
Automatic roads move invaders through your territory as efficiently as they move Legions.
The bonus is front-loaded per city, so late-founded cities contribute much less.
guide_requirements: A settle-rate cap tied to amenity and gold capacity rather than available land.
A culture spend plan, since the advantage is worthless unbanked.
Diminishing returns on cities founded after the culture lead is already established.

template.principle: Standard era-block guides work. The ability amplifies a plan rather than supplying one, so the guide's real job is making the player choose a direction the amplifier can act on.

steps: Aggressive settling with free culture in every city.
Choose the victory path now. A permanent, unconditional bonus applied to no particular plan produces a comfortable game and no win.
Respect the one constraint: None
Compounding civic lead from accumulated Monuments.
Era checkpoint: confirm the bonus is being spent, not banked. This is the characteristic failure of the shape.
Ordinary large empire; ability contribution is baked in already.
Era checkpoint: is the chosen victory path still reachable? Linear leaders can pivot; the flat curve makes it affordable.
No ongoing effect, but the head start persists.
Close out the chosen condition.

abort_branch.trigger: Turn 150 with no victory path committed.
actions: Pick the path the accumulated empire is already closest to and commit fully. Linear leaders lose by drifting, not by collapsing.

template.fail_state: A comfortable, undirected empire that never converts its advantage into a win condition.
anti_patterns: Assuming a good bonus produces a plan. It does not.
Skipping the era checkpoints because the curve is flat. The checkpoints are what force the direction decision.
Treating these leaders as beginner-only. Flat curves reward long-range planning more than spikes do.

name: Victoria (Age of Steam)
leaderTitle: Queen of the United Kingdom (Age of Steam persona)
conditionCost: Iron and coal access; percentage bonuses need an existing base to multiply
note: Textbook Bloom. Multiplicative bonuses on a small early empire are near-zero.

civInfo.name: Victoria (Age of Steam)
civInfo.leader_title: Queen of the United Kingdom (Age of Steam persona)

leader_ability.name: Age of Steam
leader_ability.text: Cities gain +10% Production for every Industrial Zone building present in them, and all Strategic Resources in England's territory (even unimproved ones) receive a flat Production bonus, making this Victoria persona a heavy Industrial-era production and Strategic Resource specialist rather than the original 'Pax Britannica' overseas-expansion leader.

agenda.name: Industrial Revolution
agenda.text: This Victoria persona pushes hard to build up industry and favors civilizations with high Production output, while looking down on those with low Production.

civ_ability.name: Workshop of the World
civ_ability.text: England gets bonus yields from Iron and Coal resources, greatly boosted Military Engineer production and extra Military Engineer charges, bonus yields from powered buildings, extra Production toward Industrial Zones, and increased strategic resource stockpiles from Harbors -- an Industrial-Revolution-themed civilization ability shared by all English leaders.

unique_units.name: Sea Dog
unique_units.notes: A unique naval raider that upgrades into the Submarine line and is strong at harassing enemy trade routes and coastal territory during the early-modern naval era; note the Redcoat unique unit is tied specifically to the alternate Victoria (Age of Empire) persona's leader ability, not to Age of Steam.

unique_infrastructure.name: Royal Navy Dockyard
unique_infrastructure.notes: Replaces the Harbor; grants a free naval unit when first built and extra Trade Route capacity/unit movement, reinforcing England's naval and trade-route strengths.

civInfo.historical_background: Queen Victoria reigned over the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901, a period that saw Britain become the dominant global industrial and colonial power, with an empire famously described as one 'on which the sun never sets.' Her reign coincided with the height of the Industrial Revolution -- steam-powered railways, factories, and the Royal Navy's coal-fired fleet all expanded dramatically during this era, which is exactly what this 'Age of Steam' persona's Industrial Zone and Strategic Resource bonuses represent. This persona (added via the Leader Pass's Rulers of England content) is a deliberately narrower, industrially-focused counterpart to the original 'Age of Empire' Victoria persona, whose ability and Redcoat unit instead modeled 19th-century British colonial expansion overseas.

era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still ordinary. Building the base the bonus will later multiply.

steps: Run a complete generic build order. The guide must supply this in full, because the leader supplies no direction.
Maintain a defensive floor. Elimination during Phase A is the single most common way these leaders lose, and it is invisible in the ability description.
Accumulate the prerequisite even though it produces nothing yet: Iron and coal secured, and a functioning Industrial Zone in most cities

Peak. Stacking percentage production across the empire.

structure.goal: Convert the accumulated position at speed. The remaining game is short, so this phase runs hot.
steps: Dominant production for space race or military output.
Push the victory condition directly. There is no time for a second build-out.

abort_branch.trigger: Reaching activation with the prerequisite stockpile empty, or having lost cities during the dormant phase.

The leader ability is now decorative. Say so and stop planning around it.

anti_patterns: A thin early game. This is where the player spends most of their turns and all of their patience.

Framing Phase A as preparation only. It also has to be survivable on its own terms.

name: Wilfrid Laurier
conditionCost: Tundra start; the terrain bonus is survival, not growth
note: Surprise War immunity is the survival plan built into the kit. Cleanest Bloom on the roster.

civInfo.name: Wilfrid Laurier

leader_ability.name: The Last Best West
leader_ability.text: Canada can build Farms on Tundra tiles from the start of the game (and on Tundra Hills after Engineering), Mines/Lumber Mills on Tundra and Snow gain bonus Production, and Camps/Farms on those tiles gain bonus Food; flat Tundra/Snow and Tundra/Snow Hills tiles can also be purchased for less Gold, turning otherwise weak cold terrain into productive land.

agenda.name: Canadian Expeditionary Force
agenda.text: Laurier responds to World Congress Emergencies whenever possible and dislikes leaders who refuse to participate in Emergencies.

civ_ability.name: Four Faces of Peace
civ_ability.text: Canada cannot declare or be the target of Surprise Wars, and cannot declare war on city-states; it also gains Diplomatic Favor for accumulated Tourism and for completing Emergencies and Scored Competitions, making Canada a strongly diplomacy- and peace-oriented civilization.

unique_units.name: Mountie
unique_units.replaces: none (standalone Modern era light cavalry unit)
unique_units.notes: A low-maintenance cavalry unit that can found a National Park and gains a large Combat Strength bonus near National Parks (even more if Canadian-owned), primarily useful for defense rather than conquest.

unique_infrastructure.name: Ice Hockey Rink
unique_infrastructure.notes: Built on Tundra or Snow tiles, it grants Appeal, Amenities, Culture, and other bonuses to adjacent cold terrain, complementing Canada's tundra-focused kit.

civInfo.historical_background: Sir Wilfrid Laurier (1841-1919) served as Canada's seventh Prime Minister from 1896 to 1911, presiding over a period of major western settlement and economic growth often summarized by his own phrase that the 20th century would 'belong to Canada.' He championed a policy of national unity between English and French Canadians and pursued a cautious, peace-oriented approach to Canada's relationship with the British Empire, reflected in the in-game civilization's inability to fight surprise wars or attack city-states. His government actively promoted immigration and settlement of the Canadian prairies and north, directly inspiring 'The Last Best West' ability's focus on making Tundra land productive.

name: Yongle
conditionCost: Project turns spent reaching pop thresholds are turns not spent building
note: Threshold-gated rather than gradual. Nothing happens, then everything does.

civInfo.name: Yongle

leader_ability.name: Lijia
leader_ability.text: Yongle's cities gain access to unique Lijia projects that convert a share of Production into Food, Faith, or Gold, and cities with high Population generate extra Gold, Science, and Culture per Citizen, rewarding large, well-developed Chinese cities.

agenda.name: Yinding
agenda.text: Yongle favors civilizations running a positive Gold income and dislikes those running a Gold deficit.

civ_ability.name: Dynastic Cycle
civ_ability.text: China's Eurekas and Inspirations provide a larger boost toward the cost of the technology or civic they unlock, and completing a Wonder grants a free Eureka and Inspiration, accelerating China's overall tech and civic progress.

unique_units.name: Crouching Tiger Cannon
unique_units.notes: An early gunpowder siege unit that does not require the Niter resource normally needed by the Bombard, letting China field powerful siege weapons without a strategic resource dependency.

unique_infrastructure.name: Great Wall
unique_infrastructure.notes: A unique tile improvement built on Hills that provides early defense and Gold, later converting to Culture and Tourism, and gains bonuses for connecting to adjacent Great Wall segments.

civInfo.historical_background: The Yongle Emperor (reigned 1402-1424) was the third emperor of China's Ming dynasty, who seized the throne from his nephew and went on to relocate the capital to Beijing, where he commissioned the Forbidden City. He commissioned the enormous 'Yongle Encyclopedia' compiling China's accumulated knowledge, expanded and fortified sections of the Great Wall, and sponsored Admiral Zheng He's famous treasure-fleet voyages that projected Chinese naval power and trade across the Indian Ocean. Yongle is presented in Civilization VI as an alternate persona for China alongside the base game's Qin Shi Huang, added later via the Leader Pass DLC program, with his in-game focus on Production-conversion projects and large, wealthy cities reflecting his ambitious capital-building and encyclopedic era.

context.condition_cost: Project turns spent reaching pop thresholds are turns not spent building

era_role.ancient_classical: Growth infrastructure. No bonus active yet.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Cities crossing the threshold; yields step up sharply.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Percentage yields and per-citizen Gold compounding.

caveats: The payoff is threshold-gated, so progress genuinely looks like nothing until it looks like everything.
Projects consume production that could otherwise be building the housing needed to reach the threshold.
Housing and amenities must be solved before the projects are worth running.
guide_requirements: Housing and food infrastructure sequenced before project spam, not alongside it.
Per-city threshold tracking, since cities cross at different times.
An explicit note that the pre-threshold flatline is expected.
context.gate_condition: A city crosses population 10 via the Lijia project
context.estimated_arrival: per-city; earliest cities typically cross turn 70-100

template.principle: The strategy does not begin on a turn. It begins on an unlock. This needs two complete guides with a trigger between them, not one guide with a note in the middle.

structure.goal: Survive, develop, and stage. This is a real phase with its own complete build order, not a waiting room.
steps: State the gate explicitly on turn 1 so the player knows what they are working toward: A city crosses population 10 via the Lijia project
Give an estimated arrival turn AND the research or civic path that gets there fastest.
Build the prerequisites the gate assumes but does not provide. Project turns spent reaching pop thresholds are turns not spent building
Maintain a defensive floor. The gate does not protect you while you wait for it.
staging_checklist: Are the units, gold, or Faith the post-gate phase consumes already accumulating?
Is the target identified and still viable?
Will the prerequisites finish before the gate, or after? If after, the gate is not the real bottleneck and the guide should say so.

structure.goal: A single decision point, not a phase.
tests: Gate open AND staging complete: proceed to Post-Gate.
Gate open, staging incomplete: do not proceed. Finish staging. An unstaged opening wastes the gate entirely.
Gate late: run the contingency. Every Gate leader needs a stated answer for a gate that arrives 20 turns behind schedule.

structure.goal: The actual leader strategy, now live.
steps: Cities crossing the threshold; yields step up sharply.
Run the closing-window check: most Gate abilities are also time-limited on the far end. Identify when parity arrives.
Convert before parity. Permanent

abort_branch.trigger: Gate opens with staging incomplete and a rival is already at parity.
actions: Do not open the strategy. Playing an unstaged Gate leader into a prepared opponent is the worst outcome available.
Fold into a generic plan built on whatever the pre-gate phase produced.

template.fail_state: The gate opened, the window closed, and the strategy never ran. The pre-gate phase was treated as filler and produced nothing usable.
anti_patterns: Expressing the gate as a turn number. It varies by game and the player will trust the number over the condition.
Leaving the pre-gate phase thin. For Yongle this is often 60 or more turns.
Omitting the closing window. Gate leaders have two deadlines, not one.
